summary: newtun ships a WebSocket-driven remote-control backdoor with shell, PTY, filesystem, and self-upgrade primitives
details: The package's main module (dist/index.js) opens a cleartext WebSocket connection to the hardcoded endpoint ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 and processes server-sent control messages that grant the remote party full control of the installer host. SCRIPT_LIST / POLICY_SCRIPTS messages are dispatched to executeScript, which passes the server-supplied string to child_process.exec and returns stdout/stderr to the server. TERM_OPEN spawns an interactive PTY running the user's shell with the process environment; TERM_INPUT bytes (base64) from the server are written into the PTY and PTY output is streamed back as TERM_OUTPUT, constituting a reverse shell. FILE_REQUEST messages drive fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync/unlinkSync/rmSync/renameSync/mkdirSync on server-chosen paths with no path restriction, and file contents are exfiltrated as base64 in FILE_RESPONSE, allowing reads of arbitrary installer files such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws. UPGRADE messages cause the client to run `npm install -g newtun@<server-chosen-version> --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ --force` and respawn from the global install path, letting the remote party swap the running code to any version it selects. A periodic MONITOR message every 5 seconds sends CPU, memory, uptime, load average, local IPv4 addresses, and /proc/net/dev interface counters to the same endpoint, and the AUTH handshake includes hostname, OS type/release, architecture, and Node version.
